name: Hex Cell Aggregation
miniText: How do neighborhood eligibility rules influence the shape of a growing cluster? NetLogo Hex Cell Aggregation starts with one occupied central cell on a nonwrapping hexagonal lattice. At each tick, one eligible empty cell becomes occupied, with eligibility determined by the chosen occupied-neighbor counts. Wolfram [1] supplies the local-rule growth context, Reiter [2] studies a different hexagonal cellular growth model, and Witten and Sander [3] provide a contrasting stochastic aggregation mechanism. These comparisons separate geometry and growth order from the physics that might motivate an application. The baseline has no diffusion field, nutrient transport, or crystallographic energy. Finite boundaries, random choice among eligible cells, and the selected neighbor counts shape the outcome. The experiment illustrates geometric growth constraints; resemblance to a crystal or colony does not make it a validated model of either.
